messages.author: 99aa11b224ba9e9e
messages.subject: Re: Nimble build error
parts:
For better or for worse, this is a known error where the NIMBLE MCMC is finding the "slice" function from another package you have loaded (perhaps package "bbmle"?  If not that, there are other possibilities...)

This has already been fixed on the development branch of NIMBLE.  You can build and install that version locally:
> library(devtools)
> install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")
> library(nimble)

Another comment about your code: Your call (which produced the error)

Cmcmc <- buildMCMC(ModSpec)

implies a bit of a misnomer, in that the buildMCMC() command will create an *R* version of the MCMC algorithm -- also executable, although very slow.  To get a compiled (C++) version of the algorithm, you'd then have to call compileNimble.  So the usual flow (and more correct variable names) would be:

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(ModSpec)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

Let me know how this works for you.

Cheers,
Daniel

On Fri, May 6, 2016 at 9:25 AM, Daniel Turek <dtu...@berkeley.edu> wrote:
For better or for worse, this is a known error where the NIMBLE MCMC is finding the "slice" function from another package you have loaded (perhaps package "bbmle"?  If not that, there are other possibilities...)

This has already been fixed on the development branch of NIMBLE.  You can build and install that version locally:
> library(devtools)
> install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")
> library(nimble)

Another comment about your code: Your call (which produced the error)

Cmcmc <- buildMCMC(ModSpec)

implies a bit of a misnomer, in that the buildMCMC() command will create an *R* version of the MCMC algorithm -- also executable, although very slow.  To get a compiled (C++) version of the algorithm, you'd then have to call compileNimble.  So the usual flow (and more correct variable names) would be:

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(ModSpec)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

Let me know how this works for you.

Cheers,
Daniel
